description: A ransomware attack originating from a malicious email attachment resulted in malware execution on an employee workstation. The malware established command-and-control communication, performed internal reconnaissance, moved laterally across the network using compromised credentials, encrypted critical business files on multiple systems, and displayed a ransom demand. IDS alerts, firewall logs, and Windows file activity collectively indicate a coordinated ransomware operation impacting enterprise resources.

attack_steps.description: User opened a malicious email attachment disguised as an invoice document.
Macro executed PowerShell payload which downloaded ransomware binary.
IDS detected malicious PowerShell activity and ransomware indicators.
Compromised host initiated outbound communication with known malicious infrastructure.
Malware attempted credential dumping from memory.
Attacker used harvested credentials to access file server and additional workstations.
Unusual access to thousands of files detected across shared drives.
Ransomware encrypted documents, spreadsheets, databases, and archives.
Ransom note created on affected systems demanding cryptocurrency payment.

rule_1.name: IDS Malware Alert Correlation
rule_1.description: Correlates IDS malware alerts with suspicious endpoint activity.

rule_2.name: Firewall Command and Control Detection
rule_2.description: Correlates outbound traffic to known malicious IPs and domains.

rule_3.name: Lateral Movement Detection
rule_3.description: Identifies suspicious SMB authentication and movement between hosts.

rule_4.name: Mass File Modification Activity
rule_4.description: Detects abnormal volume of file access and modification events.

rule_5.name: Encryption and Ransom Note Correlation
rule_5.description: Correlates encryption activity with ransom note creation.

mitre_attack.description: Malicious email attachment used for initial compromise.
PowerShell used to download and execute malware.
Malware payload downloaded from external infrastructure.
Files encrypted to disrupt business operations.

recommended_actions.description: Immediately disconnect infected endpoints and servers from the network.
Disable compromised accounts and block SMB communication where possible.
Block identified malicious IP addresses and domains at firewall and DNS layers.
Collect memory dumps, logs, malware samples, and system snapshots.
Verify integrity and availability of offline and immutable backups.
Restore affected systems from clean backups after eradication.
Reset passwords for all potentially compromised accounts.
Deploy enhanced detection rules for ransomware indicators and persistence mechanisms.

executive_summary: On June 5, 2026, SentinelGPT detected a critical ransomware incident originating from a malicious email attachment opened by a finance department employee. The malware executed PowerShell commands, established communication with known malicious infrastructure, harvested credentials, and moved laterally to enterprise file servers. More than 10,000 files were encrypted and a ransom demand was issued. Correlated IDS alerts, firewall traffic, and Windows file activity confirmed a coordinated ransomware attack. The incident received a risk score of 98/100 due to active encryption, lateral movement, business impact, and potential data loss. Immediate containment, system isolation, backup validation, and recovery operations are required to minimize operational disruption and restore affected services.
